dCapEnemy_c's members straddle two modules -- the only class in the ROM's 403 that does. Ten ordinary members, C2 and D1 are in arm9 (0x02005d94..0x02006588, config/arm9/delinks.txt); only D2 (0x020aedbc) and D0 (0x020aedf4) are in ov002. This entry is the ov002 half and claims nothing outside it. The span is bounded below by ov002/dEnemyBase_c (31 functions, ending exactly at 0x020aedbc) and above by the promoted ov002/da1up_c at 0x020aee40.
notes: Generated by tools/tubuild.py create, then rewritten by hand: the generator concatenated both legacy shard bodies and so emitted TWO definitions of `dCapEnemy_c::~dCapEnemy_c()`, which is a redefinition error. mwccarm emits D1, D2 and D0 from ONE out-of-line definition, so the TU carries a single definition and D0's `// @symbol` marker is parked at its ROM ordinal above an explanatory body.

NOT PROMOTABLE TODAY, and the refusal is the tool's own. `tubuild.py promote --dry-run` refuses with: 'manifest status is not link-verified or data-verified' and 'the promotion-ready status is not the recorded linkcheck result'. linkcheck returns scratch-link-verified, not link-verified, because the single dtor definition unavoidably also emits _ZN11dCapEnemy_cD1Ev -- a real, licensed arm9 function at 0x0200651c that src/_ZN11dCapEnemy_cD1Ev.cpp still owns -- and the scratch link only succeeds because the harness deadstrips it from the SCRATCH object before linking. Production does no such surgery. This is the key-function case tubuild.py's own ladder comment calls out: 'a key-function TU cannot [become link-verified], until phase F'. Do not route around this by licensing D1 in this entry: it is in a different module and one object's sections link into one module.

dCapEnemy_c is the ONLY class of the ROM's 403 whose destructor variants straddle two modules, so nothing else in the tree is blocked by this and no landed manifest claims a D0 without its D1 (censused: 0 of 199 entries).

PRODUCTION WALL, measured 2026-09-22, sharper than the promote --dry-run refusal above. After tools/tu_promote.py applies cleanly, rombuild fails the intact TU link control with: 'isolate: compiler-only deadstrip refused: _ZN11dCapEnemy_cD1Ev: duplicate deadstrip needs vague linkage, got STB_GLOBAL'. Reproduced twice. The cause is linkage, not bookkeeping: tools/objisolate.py requires STB_LOPROC to deadstrip a homed duplicate, and the out-of-line definition that supplies the ov002-homed D2 co-emits D1 at STB_GLOBAL. all_symbol_homes puts D1 at arm9 0x0200651c while D2 and D0 sit in ov002 (0x020aedbc, 0x020aedf4), so ov002 can never own D1 and it cannot be licensed here. ALL THREE dispositions were measured and all refuse: deadstrip-duplicate gives the STB_GLOBAL error; plain deadstrip is rejected because D1 has a configured ROM home; removing the row gives 'unlicensed content in text-only multi-symbol object'. THE DESTRUCTOR SOURCE-FORM LEVER DOES NOT HELP -- six forms probed against the pinned compiler, and whenever the destructor gets vague linkage mwccarm stops emitting D2 altogether, folding it into D1: header declaration plus out-of-line definition emits D1, D2 and D0 with D1 GLOBAL; an inline empty body in the header, an inline body plus a derived dtor, 'inline' on the out-of-line definition with or without an odr-use, and a declared 'inline virtual' with an out-of-line definition all emit only D1 and D0 at LOPROC. There is no cell that yields a strippable D1 and a D2 together, and D2 is half this TU. production_mode intact-object is not an escape either: intact mode does not deadstrip, so the strong D1 would enter the ov002 link as a live duplicate of the arm9 owner. THE NARROW FIX IS TOOL-SIDE, and belongs in its own PR: teach objisolate that a deadstrip-duplicate whose canonical home is in a DIFFERENT module is safe at STB_GLOBAL, since an ov002 object can never supply an arm9 address and the owning source still does. Reconstruction quality is not the issue -- tubuild verify reports 2 of 2 MATCH, objisolate clean, reloc-destinations clean, TEXT-VERIFIED, emission order ROM-ascending, exactly one unlicensed symbol.

The cartridge owns D1 in a DIFFERENT module, arm9:0x0200651c kind:function(arm,size=0x38), where it fills slot 16 of _ZTV11dCapEnemy_c (0x021082c4); src/_ZN11dCapEnemy_cD1Ev.cpp still holds that arm9 delinks entry as `complete`.
